issues.description: Template StockIngredient class provides a getter named retrieveQuantity(), but other template classes (Stock, Main comments) and the solution expect/getQuantity(). This mismatch in the method signature (name) prevents the template from compiling and confuses students about the required getter naming (the problem statement explicitly asks to "add getters for all the private fields").
issues.suggested_fix: Rename retrieveQuantity() in the template StockIngredient to getQuantity() (matching the rest of the template and the solution), or add a getQuantity() delegating to retrieveQuantity(). This aligns the template with the problem statement's expectation of standard getters and with other classes that call getQuantity().

issues.description: The getter for the StockIngredient quantity is named retrieveQuantity() in the template, while the rest of the code and the solution use the conventional getQuantity() name (and the problem statement asks students to add getters for private fields). This mismatch makes it hard for students to map the requirement (add getters) to the provided template and will cause compilation/runtime confusion because Stock and other code expect getQuantity().
issues.suggested_fix: Rename the template's StockIngredient.retrieveQuantity() to getQuantity() (and keep its behavior). This matches the getter naming convention, aligns with the problem statement's request for getters, and is consistent with references in Stock, Main, and the solution. Alternatively, update all references to use retrieveQuantity(), but using getQuantity() is recommended for clarity and convention.
